meta.analysis: mesh-based classification of the 195 unrouted support contacts + 49 quality-bearing residuals, Weeping Treant v1.2, engine.run cfg SupportConfig(lift_mm=3.0)
meta.mesh: treant_real_copy.stl, 576026 faces, centered by -(bounds_min+bounds_max)/2 (matches engine/pickle frame); non-watertight (contains() unreliable, so tests are ray-based and normal-agnostic)

method.engine_reproduction: engine.run re-run deterministically (all seeds fixed) on the real-copy STL; unrouted indices reproduce the pickle's 195 EXACTLY and verify counts match (28 minima/21 births/144 islands). contacts[] (omitted from the pickle) thereby recovered with positions.
method.ray_backend: pure trimesh RayMeshIntersector (rtree broadphase; no embree). Local-crop submesh (R=10mm) for clearance/corridor; full mesh only to confirm enclosure, in tiny ray batches. Peak RSS < 1 GB.
method.normal_agnostic: STL winding is inconsistent (loaded process=False); every ray cast from p+dir*0.05mm so into-solid directions self-terminate and into-air directions escape -- no stored normal trusted.

classes.INTERNAL: 0 of 300 full-sphere rays escape to infinity on the FULL mesh from the contact -> enclosed / not visible from outside
classes.GROOVE_BLOCKED: not internal AND no approach direction admits the thinnest-strut swept envelope (radius min_shoot_r+standoff=0.95mm) clear for the stub length (2.5mm): any support tip collides with adjacent model within the envelope
classes.OPEN_BUT_UNREACHED: not internal, not groove-blocked: an admissible support corridor exists; routing simply did not reach it
classes.EFFECTIVELY_REDUNDANT: orthogonal annotation kept alongside the class: nearest LIVE support member surface <=0.5mm (already held by a neighbor)

internal_verification.method: dense-direction escape test (300/800/2000 fib dirs, full mesh) + vertical shell-crossing counts (multiple_hits rays straight up/down).
internal_verification.result: every INTERNAL point tested has 0 escapes at ALL of 300/800/2000 directions (no slot narrower than ~4.5deg missed) and sits under MANY surface crossings both up and down (e.g. idx691 up=14/dn=238, idx537 up=261/dn=59, idx2 up=3/dn=45) -> buried inside stacked interpenetrating shells, not a sampling artifact.
internal_verification.controls: external points scale with density (stranded overhang #2: 87->226->576 esc; far-exterior 297->1995; model-center 833) confirming the test finds escapes when they exist.
internal_verification.interpretation: the STL is a NON-WATERTIGHT assembly of overlapping organic primitives (branches/bark/foliage) that interpenetrate; the engine's face-based overhang/island perception seeds contacts on down-facing faces that are actually INTERIOR to the solid union. These print as solid, not as exposed overhangs -> no print risk, but they inflate the unrouted/minima/island-birth counts.

priority1_stranded_overhang.mesh_class: GROOVE-BLOCKED (external: 87->576 escapes with density; genuinely stranded, nearest live member 10.24mm)
priority1_stranded_overhang.verdict: CONFIRM as the top real risk (external, unsupported ~10mm). CAVEAT: local clearance is tight -- the thinnest standard strut envelope (r0.95mm) collides within ~0.8mm, so use a FINE-tip manual support placed at a favorable angle.

priority2_crown_tip_cluster.mesh_class: INTERNAL (0/2000-dir escapes; buried in interpenetrating crown geometry)
priority2_crown_tip_cluster.verdict: RETRACT/DOWNGRADE. #4 and #5 are enclosed interior points, not exposed overhangs -- they cannot and need not be supported. The crown-tip float earlier flagged here is a perception artifact of overlapping geometry, not a print risk.

manual_support_reverdict.net: Of the two manual supports recommended, ONE (#2) is confirmed and ONE (#4/#5) is retracted. The genuine external reach gap that DOES deserve attention instead is the OPEN-BUT-UNREACHED set led by #9 (11.6,-19.0,32.2) and the broad down-facing overhang at (-19.5,13.2,-11.7).
